issues.legal_issue: The terms covering a company’s officers and employees include former officers and employees who wrongfully retain company property after their employment ends.
material_facts: The respondents had been allotted company quarters for use during their employment.
After retiring, the respondents did not vacate or return the quarters despite being required to do so.
issues.conclusion: A former officer or employee can fall within the scope of the provision dealing with wrongful withholding of company property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 630(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 1956 applies to wrongful withholding of company property after employment ends. In Baldev Krishna Sahi v. Shipping Corporation of India Ltd., the Court held that the terms “officer or employee” are not restricted to current officers or employees; Amrit Lal Chum v. Devoprasad Dutta Roy likewise recognized that wrongful retention of company property after termination of employment is an offence under the section. The provision should be construed broadly and liberally to advance its purpose of enabling the company to retrieve its property.

predicates.company_property_was_provided_during_emp: The company provided its property to a worker for use during the worker’s employment.
predicates.former_worker_wrongfully_retained_it_aft: After the employment ended, the former worker wrongfully kept the company’s property instead of returning it.
predicates.criminal_proceeding_concerns_company_pro: A criminal proceeding concerns the worker’s alleged wrongful obtaining or withholding of company property.

issues.definition: When a criminal proceeding concerns company property provided during employment and wrongfully retained by a former worker after employment ends, the former worker is within the scope of the wrongful-retention offence.

issues.legal_issue: Wrongful withholding of company property is a continuing offence for limitation purposes for as long as the property remains withheld.
material_facts: The respondents retained company quarters after their retirement and did not return them despite being required to do so.
The company filed criminal complaints more than six months after the respondents retired, while the quarters remained unreturned.
The complaints alleged wrongful withholding under the Companies Act and were dismissed as time-barred on the view that the offence was complete when the respondents failed to vacate after retirement.
issues.conclusion: The offence of wrongful withholding under section 630 is continuing until the property is delivered up or refunded, so the complaints were not barred by limitation while the wrongful retention continued.
issues.legal_principle: Whether an offence is continuing depends on the language creating it, its nature, and its purpose. Section 630(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 1956 makes wrongful withholding of company property an offence, and section 630(2) contemplates an order to deliver up or refund the property. Under sections 468 and 472 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, limitation applies to qualifying offences, but for a continuing offence a fresh period begins at every moment the offence continues. Section 473 permits cognizance after limitation where the statutory conditions are met. The Court applied State of Bihar v. Deokaran Nenshi and Bhagirath Kanoria v. State of Madhya Pradesh, and overruled W.M.I. Cranes Ltd. v. G.G. Advani on this point.

predicates.criminal_complaint_concerns_wrongful_com: A criminal complaint alleges that a worker or former worker wrongfully obtained or withheld company property.
predicates.company_property_remained_wrongfully_wit: The company’s property was still being wrongfully withheld when the criminal complaint was filed.

issues.definition: If a criminal complaint concerns wrongful withholding of company property and the property remains wrongfully withheld when the complaint is filed, the complaint is not time-barred while that withholding continues.
